_comment: Catalogue for Test simulations. Four levels: Home -> Test simulations -> category -> item -> case.
A case starts from its mode's defaults (GET /api/defaults/{mode}) and applies
`overrides` on top, so it only states what it changes. Unknown override paths
are reported rather than silently ignored.
An item with no cases and `available: false` is a reduction the engine tests
but the web API cannot express, because the term it isolates has no off
switch in the setup schema. `evidence` points at what does cover it.
Served as a static asset and deliberately NOT part of the qpsim source
manifest, so editing this catalogue costs no recertification.

An `expect` block states a closed form and how to check it: read `observable` from the run summary and compare against `reference` (another summary field, so the target is computed rather than typed) within `rel_tol`, or with `comparison` for an inequality.

A case may name a `benchmark`: the server then checks the whole run against that closed form pointwise and returns the curve, the residual and a verdict. The formula, tier, tolerance and convergence evidence come from /api/benchmarks, not from this file, so the claim shown before a run is the same string checked after it.

categories.title: Single term examples
categories.blurb: One term of the kinetic equations on its own. All ten now run. The two phonon source terms are the phonon side of the collision channels rather than separate processes, so switching one side off breaks energy conservation on purpose — those cases warn.

items.title: Diffusion
items.blurb: Quasiparticles spread along the strip and nothing else acts.

cases.title: Diffusion against its eigenmode decay rate
cases.summary: With no collisions and a uniform gap, N₁ leaves the divergence and each energy bin is an independent scalar heat equation; a cell-centred cosine is an exact eigenfunction of the Laplacian AND of the discrete no-flux stencil, so its amplitude decays as a pure exponential at D_eff(E)k². The energy dependence of that rate is the whole content of the (p,q) dressing, which is why the curve is taken over energy rather than time.

overrides.material.name: Al
overrides.initial.expression: params['f0'] * (1.0 + params['a'] * np.cos(params['m'] * np.pi * x) * np.cos(params['n'] * np.pi * y))

cases.title: Diffusion alone
cases.summary: Injection at the left end with both collision channels off. Transport is the only term that shapes the profile, and it nearly flattens it: left/right = 1.04.

cases.title: The same strip with transport off
cases.summary: D_0 = 0 makes the flux coefficient identically zero, so the cells stop talking to each other and the injected quasiparticles pile up: left/right = 544 instead of 1.06. Run it against the case above.

items.title: Quasiparticle-phonon scattering
items.blurb: Quasiparticles move up and down in energy by emitting and absorbing phonons. Nothing creates or destroys them.

cases.title: Scattering against its closed-form out-rate
cases.summary: At T_bath -> 0 the phonon occupation vanishes and the scattering operator can only move a quasiparticle down in energy, so the highest occupied cell of a column has no source above it: its gain term is identically zero and, once the excess is small enough for Pauli blocking to be negligible, its equation is a linear decay at a constant rate. That rate's continuum limit is the Kaplan scattering-out integral, which is elementary. Five columns seeded at five energies with D_0 = 0 keeps them independent, so one run measures five different rates against five closed forms.

cases.title: Scattering alone
cases.summary: Start thermal with recombination and both drives off. Scattering has thermal as its own fixed point, so nothing moves: x_qp holds at 2.2243e-10.

expect.reason: Scattering satisfies detailed balance against a thermal phonon bath, so the Fermi-Dirac distribution is its fixed point and nothing evolves.

items.title: Recombination and pair breaking
items.blurb: Two quasiparticles annihilate into a phonon above 2Δ, and that phonon breaks a pair. The only term that changes quasiparticle number.

cases.title: Recombination against the two-body 1/t law
cases.summary: With scattering, both drives and transport removed and the phonons pinned at the bath, recombination is the only term left, and it moves no quasiparticle between energy bins (Kaplan Eq. 8: the partner is booked in the partner's own bin). A one-cell excess therefore stays in its cell and the NE-dimensional system collapses to dg/dt = -R g^2, whose exact solution is the two-body 1/t law. R is written down from elementary BCS cell integrals with no free parameter, so the height AND the rate of the whole curve are predicted rather than fitted.

cases.title: Recombination alone
cases.summary: The same start with scattering off instead. The pair channel also holds thermal, to the last few digits of the scattering-only answer.

expect.reason: The pair channel also balances at thermal: emission into the bath and reabsorption from it cancel bin by bin.

items.title: Sub-gap photon drive
items.blurb: Photons below 2Δ shuffle quasiparticles in energy without creating any.

cases.title: Sub-gap drive against the exact ladder solution
cases.summary: The sub-gap term is a jump operator in energy, so with the photon step chosen above half the grid span (N_E/2 <= m < N_E) no bin has both an up and a down partner and the operator decomposes into independent two-rung ladders. Each ladder conserves B·f_a + A·f_b, which reduces it to one scalar Riccati equation with an elementary solution. No linearisation is used: the Pauli factors are carried in full, so the closed form is exact for arbitrary occupation and at every grid spacing, and the only approximation left in the run is the ETD2 time step.

cases.title: Sub-gap drive alone
cases.summary: Both collision channels off, so the drive is the only term. It redistributes f in energy while the number stays put.

expect.reason: The sub-gap channel moves quasiparticles in energy without creating or destroying any, so the number is conserved exactly while the distribution reshapes.

items.title: Pair-breaking photon drive
items.blurb: Photons above 2Δ create new quasiparticles.

cases.title: Pair breaking against its exactly linear growth
cases.summary: At f = 0 every block of the pair-breaking photon integral except pair generation carries an explicit factor of f — both scattering gains at the partner index, the whole loss rate, and the pair-recombination loss on top of it — so df/dt at zero occupation is the single f-independent term S_i. With both collision channels off, the phonons pinned and Δ frozen, S_i is the entire right-hand side, so f is linear in t and the per-bin slope is the closed form. The reflection partner is an exact lattice reflection here, j(i) = 209 − i rather than a rounding, and the cell measures are elementary integrals, so S_i is written rather than quadratured.

cases.title: Pair-breaking drive alone
cases.summary: Creation with no sink of any kind: x_qp climbs from 2.2e-10 to 1.36e-05 and would keep going. There is no steady state to find.

expect.reason: Photons above 2Δ create quasiparticles and nothing removes them, so the number can only grow. There is no steady state.

items.title: External injection
items.blurb: Quasiparticles fed in from outside the film at a rate you specify.

cases.title: Injection against its exact accumulation rate
cases.summary: With D₀ = 0, both collision channels off and no photon drives, the right-hand side is the source alone and does not depend on f, so f is exactly linear in t. The stepper reproduces that exactly rather than approximately: loss = 0 collapses the ETD1 weight (1−e^{−μdt})/μ to dt, the ETD2 corrector averages two identical constant rates, and the weighted-balance projection finds its target already met, so each step is f ← f + dt·S.

cases.title: Injection alone
cases.summary: Transport off and both collision channels off, so nothing spreads or removes what is injected. It accumulates at the left end: left/right = 1031.

items.title: Phonon scattering source
items.blurb: Books the phonons emitted and absorbed when quasiparticles scatter. It is the phonon side of the scattering channel, not a separate process.

cases.title: The phonon scattering source against its affine relaxation
cases.summary: TIER, PRECISELY: T1 in the time law and T2-equivalent in the per-ω rate constant. The exponential flow is written from the physics, but a_ω and b_ω are rebuilt from the same finite-volume formulas the engine uses and would reproduce a wrong kernel unchanged, so the weaker label ships. With the quasiparticle occupation held still the phonon equation is exactly affine and diagonal in ω, so it has an elementary solution: one exponential per frequency, with rate 1/τ_l + |b_ω| and fixed point (a_ω + n_B/τ_l)/(1/τ_l + |b_ω|). The engine integrates that same affine flow exactly (advance_phonons composes exp(Bh) with φ₁(Bh) through expm1), so there is no time-discretisation error to remove and the whole residual is the frozen-occupation reduction plus arithmetic. What the curve tests per ω is the combination a_ω + b_ω n_B(ω,T_bath) — the phonon-side collision integral evaluated at the bath occupation — over 127 frequencies at once.

cases.title: Quasiparticles scatter, phonons do not record it
cases.summary: The scattering channel on for the quasiparticles and off for the phonons. Energy leaves one population without arriving in the other, so the ledger does not balance: x_qp = 2.257e-03 against 2.261e-03 symmetric. The interface warns; there is no thermal fixed point here.

cases.title: Phonons record what quasiparticles no longer do
cases.summary: The same split the other way round: the phonon source is driven by an f that scattering no longer moves. x_qp = 2.851e-03.

items.title: Phonon recombination source
items.blurb: Books the 2Δ phonons recombination emits and pair breaking reabsorbs. This is what phonon trapping is made of.

cases.title: The recombination source against Kaplan's S+
cases.summary: With f held at a constant A the pair convolution factorises: every emission weight is A² and every pair-breaking weight is (1−A)², so a_ph and b_ph are the same line integral J(ω) times two known numbers, and the phonon equation becomes an affine ODE with constant coefficients whose solution is an exponential approach to −a/b. J(ω) is the Kaplan pair integral truncated to the energy band the grid represents, evaluated here by an independent Gauss-Legendre quadrature; the engine evaluates it as a midpoint sum over the pair lattice and, on the spatial route, applies no endpoint correction to it, so the two are genuinely different computations of the same number.

cases.title: Recombination on the quasiparticle side only
cases.summary: Pairs recombine but the 2Δ phonons are never booked, so nothing can break them again and trapping disappears: x_qp = 1.733e-03 against 2.261e-03 with the loop closed.

items.title: Phonon-bath coupling
items.blurb: Phonons leak out of the film into the substrate bath on a timescale tau_esc.

cases.title: Escape against pure exponential relaxation
cases.summary: From an empty superconductor (f ≡ 0) every scattering and recombination-emission contribution to the phonon source carries a factor of the quasiparticle density ρf and vanishes, while pair breaking carries ρ(1−f) twice and survives: a_ph ≡ 0 and b_ph = −Γ_pb exactly. The phonon equation is then a constant-coefficient affine ODE per ω bin, which the engine integrates with the exact exponential map, and eliminating the source leaves a form in which τ_l appears twice — once as the rate it contributes and once as the surviving bath fraction n_∞/n_bath = τ_eff/τ_l, which is the escape term's own statement.

cases.title: Closed sector: nothing leaves
cases.summary: The phonon population solved in time with no substrate to escape to. Every frequency bin drifts away from the bath value and keeps going, because energy arrives and nothing removes it.

cases.title: The same run with escape switched on
cases.summary: Finite tau_esc pulls the phonons back toward the bath, so they settle instead of drifting. Run it against the case above: the difference is the coupling.

items.title: Self-consistent gap
items.blurb: Δ is re-solved from the occupation instead of being held fixed.

cases.title: The BCS closure against an independent solve of it
cases.summary: With every kinetic term off and D_0 = 0 each cell is frozen at the occupation it was prepared with, so the closure alone acts and its root is the finite-cutoff BCS gap at that cell's temperature. The Matsubara identity for tanh(E/2T)/E makes that root an explicit arctangent series with a Hurwitz-zeta remainder -- no quadrature rule, no engine array, no root of an engine residual.

cases.title: Gap closure alone
cases.summary: Every collision term off, so f stays thermal and only the BCS closure acts. It returns Δ = 179.342 μeV at 0.2 K, down from the 180 μeV input.

expect.reason: With every collision term off, f stays thermal and the closure must return the equilibrium gap at the bath temperature. The tolerance is set by the grid, not by taste: the finite-volume gap integral converges to Delta_eq at first order in dE, measured 4.3e-6 at 96 bins, 2.0e-6 at 192 and 1.1e-6 at 384. Refine the grid and the agreement tightens.

categories.title: Two term examples
categories.blurb: Two terms together. Pairs that need a term with no off switch are marked; the rest run.

items.title: Scattering + recombination
items.blurb: The electron-phonon collision integral on its own, with the phonons pinned at the bath. This is the smallest model this interface can build.

cases.title: Thermal equilibrium
cases.summary: The collision integral vanishes at the Fermi-Dirac distribution, so the solve should return it.

cases.title: Thermal equilibrium, cold
cases.summary: The same fixed point at 0.1 K, where the pair channel is suppressed by e^(-2Δ/kT) and the number mode gets hard to resolve.

items.title: Scattering + sub-gap drive
items.blurb: Redistribution in energy with no number channel: nothing sets how many quasiparticles there are.

items.title: Recombination + pair-breaking drive
items.blurb: Creation balanced by annihilation, with no energy relaxation between them.

cases.title: Recombination against a pair-breaking drive
cases.summary: Scattering off, so the pair channel alone has to absorb the drive. It reaches a steady state at x_qp = 1.716e-03.

items.title: Diffusion + scattering
items.blurb: Transport with energy relaxation but no number channel.
items.why: Needs recombination off while scattering stays on in the strip, which is now possible; a case has not been pinned yet.

items.title: Recombination + its phonon source
items.blurb: The trapping loop closed on itself: recombination phonons breaking pairs again before they leave.
items.why: Needs scattering off on both sides of the loop.

items.title: Self-consistent gap + recombination
items.blurb: The gap responding to a population that only the pair channel controls.

categories.title: Literature reproductions
categories.blurb: The conditions of a published point, set up so you can vary them. These are not the certified figure reproductions: those are full sweeps with pinned baselines and provenance, and they live in the validation suite.

items.title: Fischer & Catelani 2023
items.blurb: Table I aluminium under a sub-gap drive, with the phonons solved at finite escape time.

cases.title: Fig. 6, one operating point
cases.summary: The single point the 66-point Fig. 6 sweep is built from.

items.title: Marchegiani 2025
items.blurb: The gap-asymmetric junction rate-equation layer at its shipped defaults.

cases.title: Parity switching
cases.summary: Parity-switching rates against the junction parameters.

items.title: Driven steady states
items.blurb: A drive balanced by recombination, which is what fixes the amplitude.

cases.title: Sub-gap photon drive
cases.summary: A real sub-gap drive at the published Fischer photon number. It reshapes f near the gap edge; x_qp settles at 1.007e-05.

cases.title: Pair-breaking photon drive
cases.summary: An above-gap drive creating quasiparticles, with recombination the only sink. x_qp = 1.729e-03.

cases.title: Phonon trapping
cases.summary: The same drive with the phonons solved at finite escape time: x_qp = 2.261e-03 against 1.729e-03 pinned. That 31% is the trapping.

items.title: Time dependence
items.blurb: The transient solver, with the phonons frozen at the bath.

cases.title: Photon kick
cases.summary: Start thermal, switch a real pair-breaking drive on at t = 0, and watch f climb.

items.title: Spatial transport
items.blurb: The 1D strip. A1 is the dirty-limit operator; the others are labelled diagnostics, not alternative physics.

cases.title: Uniform strip, A1
cases.summary: A uniform gap, so every energy diffuses independently at D_0/N_1(E).

cases.title: Same strip, legacy operator C
cases.summary: At a uniform gap C shares A1's rate and differs only in conserved density. The two separate once the gap varies.

cases.title: Step gap interface
cases.summary: Two regions of unequal gap joined at one face. Quasiparticles collect on the low-gap side.

items.title: Two-dimensional geometry
items.blurb: The unified spatial core. The mask sets the dimensionality, so the same mode covers 2-D, the 1-D strip and a single 0-D cell.

cases.title: Square film, nothing escapes
cases.summary: A 16x16 film with reflective edges. Quasiparticles stay in, so the film settles at its thermal value.

cases.title: The same film with an absorbing rim
cases.summary: Identical but the edge absorbs. Quasiparticles now leave the film and the population collapses far below thermal. Run it against the case above.

cases.title: The 1-D strip as a one-cell-wide mask
cases.summary: rows = 1 makes the 5-point stencil the 3-point chain exactly. This is the same physics the dedicated 1D strip mode solves, reached by choosing the geometry rather than the mode.
